commands.summary: decisions/0046-incremental-rog-convergence-and-contribution-reuse-contract.md binds: full build remains the correctness oracle; only semantic extraction is contribution-incremental (governance+physical always rebuilt globally); correctness authorities are limited to repository-relative path + content digest + an explicit semantic-compatibility identity (never Git diff, mtime, watcher events, or parser caches); delta classification is add/modify/delete only, with rename treated as delete+add and no fabricated persistent identity; required fallback behavior per baseline state; a durable-replacement safety upgrade (rename-based backup and rollback); and deterministic recomputed-not-bookkept coverage aggregation. Extends Decision 0044 with two additive optional schema-v2 fields; no schema-major bump.

69/69 tests pass (43 pre-existing unchanged + 26 new incremental tests), including the full ROG-012 mutation-class equivalence matrix -- addition, declaration edit, non-semantic edit (digest changes, symbol IDs proven unchanged), delete (symbols/edges/coverage entry removed), rename-as-delete-plus-add (no fabricated identity), manifest change (Cargo.toml/pyproject.toml/package.json, converges through the global physical rebuild), relationship change (old import fact removed, new one appears), governance change (single-file reparse, not mass reparsing), parser-failure introduction (only the broken file reparsed, unrelated contributions survive, freshness Partial), parser-failure recovery (Partial clears, converges to a clean rebuild), binary/oversized policy transitions (no stale contribution survives a normal->binary->normal round trip), unsupported-file addition/deletion (truthful coverage), a true no-op (rog/manifest.json byte-unchanged, zero reparses), a ROG-only/excluded-tree no-op proof, a 100-file observable reuse proof (1 file changed -> exactly 1 reparse, 99 reuses, output byte-identical to a clean full rebuild), compatibility-mismatch/schema-v1/old-v2-without-incremental-metadata/corrupt-baseline/unsupported-schema fallback behavior (each producing the documented mode/fallback_reason, never mislabeling a full rebuild as incremental), the WI057 bounded-git-invocation re-check (<=4), and a fault-injection proof that a forced failure on the final install rename leaves the prior durable graph byte-recoverable rather than half-written or lost. Every equivalence test compares the incremental candidate against an independently, cleanly built full rebuild of the same final state byte-for-byte (every manifest field, every node/edge shard's bytes), not just matching counts.

Full workspace green (repopact-graph 69, repopact-desktop-api 11 including the WI057 process/scaling tests, repopact-validation 49, repopact-mutation 15, all others unaffected); repeated after a performance-driven refactor (below) with the same result.
Clean; one pre-existing formatting drift in an unrelated repopact-mutation test file was picked up incidentally by a workspace-wide fmt run and committed separately as a no-behavior-change chore.

commands.command: Performance-correctness fix discovered while gathering engineering timing evidence
commands.summary: incremental::update was found to recompute the full SourceProjection twice per call (once to compare fingerprints/compute the delta, again inside the always-global governance+physical rebuild) -- on a large repository the projection walk (content-hashing every projected file) dominates wall time far more than semantic parsing does, so this roughly doubled every incremental update's cost. Fixed by splitting RepositoryGraph::build_governance_and_physical into a projection-computing wrapper (unchanged behavior, used by the full build) and build_governance_and_physical_with_projection, which incremental::update now calls with the projection it already has. All 69 repopact-graph tests remained green before and after; committed as its own logical commit.

commands.command: Real RepoPact-scale engineering timing evidence (engineering validation only, not S8/R1, not claimed as ROG-032 evidence)
commands.summary: On a disposable ~5,100-file copy of RepoPact's own live checkout (via the raw engine stdio protocol, graph.build then graph.update): full build 25.2s (755 files considered, 107 semantically complete, node_count=4574, edge_count=6237); a subsequent no-op update 24.0s (mode=no_op, semantic_reparsed=0, semantic_reused=755, byte-identical manifest); a single-file change 21.3s after the projection-duplication fix (mode=incremental, files_modified=1, semantic_reparsed=1, semantic_reused=754, freshness=fresh). All three measurements are the same order of magnitude because the source-projection content-hashing walk, not semantic parsing or governance/physical construction, dominates wall time on this fixture -- an honest finding, not a target this checkpoint claims to have optimized away; a non-authoritative digest-cache acceleration layer (explicitly not a correctness input, per Decision 0046 section 3) is a candidate for a future phase, not attempted here.

An identical fixture (5 files: Rust module with a test, Python class, TypeScript interface -- hash-verified byte-identical by SHA-256 of every file) was independently built to s0 and mutated to s1 (2 files added, 2 modified including one blank-line/comment-only edit, 1 file renamed) via the raw engine stdio protocol on native Windows (C:\Projects\repopact checkout) and a freshly re-synced Linux-native WSL2 Debian 13 checkout (~/repopact-linux, rebuilt from the pushed commits, never /mnt/c/...). Result: byte-for-byte identical graph.update output (mode=incremental, baseline/current fingerprints, files_added=2/files_modified=2/files_deleted=1/files_unchanged=2, semantic_reparsed=4/semantic_reused=2, final_node_count=19/final_edge_count=25, freshness=fresh) and every one of 12 node and 14 edge shard SHA-256 hashes in the final manifest. No macOS execution occurred or is claimed.

A dedicated incremental-specific test (update_does_not_exceed_the_wi057_bounded_git_invocation_count) confirms graph.update stays within the existing <=4-Git-invocations-per-snapshot bound; incremental::update performs zero additional Git invocations of its own (delta computation and previous-contribution reuse are pure durable-graph reads plus in-memory comparison, not Git or filesystem-diff operations).
Dashboard regenerated and committed; canonical repopact validate passes with zero diagnostics on the live (graph-disabled) checkout.

closeout.decision_0046: accepted -- full build remains the oracle; only semantic extraction is contribution-incremental; two additive optional schema-v2 fields (FileCoverageEntry.source_digest, Manifest.semantic_compatibility); durable-replacement rename-with-rollback safety
closeout.delta_representation: add/modify/delete classified from repository-relative path + SourceProjection content digest only; rename/move is delete-at-old-path plus add-at-new-path with no fabricated persistent identity carried across
closeout.semantic_compatibility_identity: graph_schema_major + explicit pipeline_version/resource_policy_version constants + adapter_versions; any mismatch (or its absence on an older v2 baseline) forces a conservative full rebuild rather than risking reuse against changed extraction behavior
closeout.contribution_architecture: semantic::build_file_contribution is the single per-file contribution-generation primitive; a full build calls it for every projected file, incremental update calls it only for added/modified files and reuses a prior file's nodes/edges (read back from durable shards, grouped by each item's existing source.path) for unchanged files; semantic::aggregate_coverage recomputes SemanticCoverage's aggregates deterministically from the final per-file inventory in both paths
closeout.update_modes: no_op (true no-op, rog/ not rewritten, semantic_reparsed=0) / incremental (delta-based reuse) / full_fallback (never mislabeled incremental) -- fallback_reason values observed and tested: graph_absent, schema_v1_upgrade, incremental_metadata_absent, semantic_compatibility_mismatch, corrupt_baseline_full_rebuild; an unsupported schema major fails closed (no write) rather than falling back

ac_notes.ROG-012: Every change class the AC text names -- additions, edits, deletes, renames/moves where supported, manifest changes, relationship changes, and parser-failure recovery -- is covered by a dedicated test proving byte-for-byte canonical equivalence between an incremental update's output and a clean full rebuild of the same final state, plus a 100-file observable-reuse proof and a cross-platform (Windows/Linux) proof of the same property. Marked satisfied.
ac_notes.ROG-030: Schema versioning, unsupported-major fail-closed behavior, and v1-remains-readable compatibility were already proven by the foundation/semantic checkpoints; this checkpoint adds and tests real migration/fallback behavior (schema-v1-to-v2 upgrade via full rebuild only, no in-place migration; old-v2-without-incremental-metadata and corrupt-baseline fallback), which is what the AC's 'compatibility/migration behavior' language specifically calls for. Reassessed conservatively and marked satisfied on that concrete evidence.
